checks.Title: Seduce, don't just observe
checks.Evidence: The opening green-room texture (chain lamp, taped cable rivers, Mona's light-strip pulsing amber to white, Rill's wrist-seam dampeners, Dayo's poet-naming of Glass/Fade/Candor) is genuinely seductive lived-in-wrong detail that pulls before horror lands — but once the Candor kicks in and the telepathy/horror machinery starts, the prose shifts almost entirely into thriller-mechanics mode (turns counted, read-outputs relayed like tactical comms) and stops finding new strange-beautiful textures to seduce with.
checks.Fix: Thread at least one or two more sensory/world-texture beats (the genemod fangs, the Thread space-elevator line, the neuretics handshake) into the escape and shootout sections so the seduction continues alongside the horror instead of yielding the floor entirely to plot mechanics.

checks.Title: Open with the world doing its work
checks.Evidence: The story opens mid-adrenaline, immediately after a set: 'The last chord was still hanging out front when Ethan Wolfe pushed through the green room door' — the plot's emotional engine (exhaustion, the Mona tension, the imminent Dayo deal) is already running in paragraph one, with no grounded, plotless entry beat of a stranger-eyed world before the character-and-stakes machinery engages.
checks.Fix: Precede this with a short beat of ordinary world-texture untouched by plot — e.g., a bouncer counting a till, a bartender restocking, the city's mundane commerce outside the club — before dropping into Ethan's post-show nerves and the band's charged dynamics.

checks.Title: Gloss first mentions in-voice, never dump
checks.Evidence: Most proprietary nouns (neuretics, CorpoNations-adjacent brand names like Waxwing Neuromedia, Fenris Ballistics, Greymark Unseen, The Low, The Thread) are dropped in via appositive or sensory action without lecturing — e.g. 'his overlay ran empty' and 'the Thread's pods barely moved against the dark, the space elevator holding its long thin line down' gloss geography cleanly in-voice. But some terms land as unglossed drops that assume prior context, like 'the dampeners in his wrists' and 'Rill went inward and the drums came out' for Glass, plus 'Zone 4' and 'Zone-4 Umami' used as if the reader already has the zone map, which risks losing a true first-timer.
checks.Fix: Add one small in-voice anchor the first time 'Zone 4' or 'The Low' appears (e.g. a short sensory or status cue showing what living in that zone means) so newcomers get their footing without a lecture.

checks.Title: Never an acronym before its term
checks.Evidence: Multiple acronyms/initialisms appear with no in-voice expansion at first use: 'AR layer' ('his overlay ran empty'), 'PA' ('a PA held together by hope'), 'NSB'-style tech term 'The Pulse' is fine as a proper noun but 'CDW submachine gun' is dropped as a bare label with no gloss of what CDW stands for, and 'FB-7' on the Fenris Ballistics Howl is presented as a model code with no expansion.
checks.Fix: Introduce each abbreviation the first time in-voice with its full term glossed naturally, e.g. 'a public-address system—a PA—held together by hope' and 'a caseless-defense-weapon carbine, a CDW, slung across his front,' before ever using the bare initials again.

checks.Title: Give the POV character one human crack
checks.Evidence: "He didn't sit. If he sat he'd stop, and if he stopped he'd feel every one of his thirty-six years land at once" and the wall imagery with Mona ("Twice in four years... they'd gotten up and built the band into a wall between them, brick by brick") crack Ethan open as a tired, aging man carrying an unspoken loss before the plot machinery starts, and he re-armors immediately by greeting Rill and deflecting Mona's "you're shaking."

checks.Title: Land one beat past the handoff
checks.Evidence: The story ends with a fully resolved diegetic 'punchline' scene: three months later, injuries healed, band back onstage, the unfinished song literally finished and sung, and Faith in the front row 'fine,' already knowing the words — a bow-tied conclusion rather than a quiet gesture past the resolution.
checks.Fix: Cut the epilogue's triumphant completeness (finished song, healed cast, crowd catching the line) and instead end on one small, unresolved physical or sensory detail — Ethan noticing the scorch mark on the table, or Faith's hand finding his in the dark without either speaking — that carries cost and unfinished weight rather than delivering closure and a happy tableau.

checks.Title: Reward re-reading without requiring it
checks.Evidence: Details like Faith reading the room 'the way you'd read a face, and whatever she found made her go quiet a beat, like a woman who'd walked into a party she already half-remembered,' the Fenris/Wolfpack shotgun joke, and Mona's light-strip going white/amber all function as complete first-pass sensory beats (mystery, irony, mood) while retroactively reframing as clues once the ending reveals Faith's telepathy and history once read.

checks.Title: Elevate, don't reconstruct
checks.Evidence: This is a dense, structurally maximal short story — a full green-room-to-shootout-to-hospital-to-epilogue arc with layered worldbuilding (neuretics, mesh handles, Fade/Glass/Candor lore, Fenris Ballistics branding, Waxwing Neuromedia signage, The Low/The Thread geography) all introduced cold, plus a telepathy reveal, two on-page deaths, a gunfight, and a three-months-later coda — none of which reads like 'tuning' an existing piece for new readers but like the entire house being built from scratch at gateway scope.
checks.Fix: Strip this back to a single contained scene (the green room before the raid, or the raid itself) and let dense worldbuilding/lore (neuretics jargon, brand names, the telepathy mechanic's rules) be trimmed or clarified in place rather than layering an entire multi-act plot with a new superpower reveal into the 'gateway' pass.

checks.Title: Orient through GLMZ's five pillars
checks.Evidence: Neuretics, nanites, and Schism-adjacent tech appear woven into texture (Ethan's neuretics pings, Mona's dampener wrists and light-strip, Rill's dampeners, the gray-zone Low), and CorpoNations-as-governance is gestured at via Waxwing Neuromedia signage and gray-zone framing of 'The Low' as ungoverned air; AIs-as-agents and the Schism itself are almost entirely absent — there is no AI character with faction/agenda anywhere in the story, and 'Schism' as a physics-breaking rift is never named or felt at all.
checks.Fix: Introduce at least one AI entity with visible stakes/faction (e.g., the venue's or mesh's AI reacting with its own agenda during the crisis) and thread in one concrete, felt reference to the Schism as a world-defining rupture, not just neuretics/nanites texture.
